_note: <Rating> — the labelled, accessible, adjustable star row (U11). ONE ADJUSTABLE ELEMENT, not five buttons: the glyphs are a11yHidden and the row announces '3 of 5 stars' through a11yValue, because a screen reader walking five identical star buttons learns nothing. HALF STEPS ARE DISPLAY-AND-ADJUST ONLY — a tap always lands on a whole star, since there is no sub-glyph hit target that behaves the same under a mouse, a finger and a D-pad — and a non-star `icon` has no half glyph in the system symbol set, so it rounds up rather than drawing the wrong shape. The per-glyph decision is `fill = clamp(score - (n - 1), 0, 1)`. THE FORMULA INPUT IS `score`, NEVER `value`: `value` is a reserved formula-input name on the web compiler and is dropped there while the native readers keep it, so a formula naming it reads null on web and the right number on iOS and Android — every glyph drew empty on the web renderer until this corpus pinned it.

cases.name: the defaults: five stars, zero score, not read-only, whole steps
the announced value is the whole contract: '3 of 5 stars'
a score past the top clamps rather than announcing '9 of 5'
a negative score clamps to zero
a score that is not a number is zero, not NaN in the utterance
max clamps to at least one glyph and rounds to a whole number of them
the glyph row is one cell per star, keyed positionally
an earned star is filled and tinted
a partly earned star draws the HALF glyph when half="true"
the same partly earned star is EMPTY when half steps are off
a three-quarter fill rounds UP to a whole star, halves or not
an unearned star is untinted, so colour is not the only signal of the boundary
a non-star icon has no half glyph, so it rounds up rather than drawing a wrong shape
a non-star icon drops the noun from the announcement rather than saying 'hearts stars'
the earned tint is caller-set and applies to earned glyphs only
readOnly is a declared display mode, so adjust and tap can both refuse
the control's own name is caller-replaceable and never collides with its value
